For every caller and sequence of deposits and cashouts where deposits are made via payable Deposit(), the reference contract only ever increases balances when msg.value > MinDeposit, so after any CashOut(uint) call the reference's balances(key) is >=  the mutant's balances(key) for all keys; the mutant inverting the Deposit conditional allows small deposits (<= MinDeposit) that the reference would have ignored, producing states where balances differ after CashOut for some fuzzed inputs.

For any caller, CashOut(uint) does not increase any address's recorded balance compared to the reference behavior: after calling CashOut on the reference contract, for every address k the reference's balances(k) is >= 0 (i.e. balances never become negative) and specifically the reference never accepts deposits of value <= MinDeposit so any small-deposit behaviour that the mutant adds can create differences — we assert the reference's balances for the caller is unchanged or nonnegative after CashOut (the mutant can produce a differing balance for some fuzzed inputs).
